spec_match.rationale: Contrasts the elements' built-in APG keyboard contract (single tab stop, arrow traversal, Escape focus-return, implicit roles) with a faithful hand-built role=menubar implementation, which is exactly the pairing the explainer motivates; the comparison table's native-side claims come from the explainer and Chromium source, not invention.

interactive.rationale: The ARIA half is a genuinely working menubar in any browser: mouse, touch, ArrowLeft/Right/Up/Down, Home/End, Enter/Space, Escape with focus return, roving tabindex, radio/checkbox aria-checked state, outside-click dismissal, all feeding a shared live command log.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index promises the native model side by side with a real working ARIA implementation; that is what renders.

edge_cases.rationale: Disabled menuitem (aria-disabled, not activatable), radio exclusivity, checkbox toggling, Tab-exit closing menus, and last-menu right-edge alignment are all implemented and exercisable.

references.rationale: Links https://chromestatus.com/feature/5206029088063488 and the APG menubar pattern.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite covers the element/IDL/popover contracts this page's native half depends on; the keyboard behavior itself is not automatable as a conformance assertion and is recorded as the page's live demonstration instead.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 verified via ?autorun: ARIA View menu opened, checkbox toggled (log shows checked=false from the defaultchecked-true start), File menu opened with visible focus ring on New, aria-expanded=true and data-open present in DOM dump, console clean, 0 overflow at true 360; the native half's keyboard model cannot run on 141.

telemetry_health.rationale: kbd-aria-menu-works asserts real ARIA activations, kbd-native-activation asserts flagged-path activations, and kbd-native-fallback-honest reports the unsupported branch separately.

design_system.rationale: ARIA menu buttons override background AND color together (bg-paper + text-black), hover uses bg-stone, focus-visible outlines everywhere, CSS variables only.

accessibility.rationale: The fallback is itself the accessibility showcase: correct menubar/menu/menuitem(radio|checkbox) roles, aria-haspopup/aria-expanded/aria-checked maintained, roving tabindex, focus return on Escape, aria-disabled soft-disable, and a live-region command log.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at 1280x1800 and true-360 (iframe harness, menus open via autorun): 0px overflow, panels stack to one column under 640px, ARIA popup menus cap at calc(100vw - 2rem) and the last submenu right-aligns to avoid the viewport edge, 44px item heights.

guidanceConsulted.query: popover anchored dropdown positioning dismissal focus
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Do not apply role=menu/menuitem unless the full arrow-key keyboard contract is implemented; use popover/anchor machinery for edge resilience where available.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The ARIA half implements the complete APG keyboard contract before claiming menu roles — precisely the guidance's mandatory condition; its position:absolute fallback (deliberately shown as the today-pattern cost) uses max-width and right-alignment to avoid viewport clipping.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible menu keyboard navigation roving tabindex aria menubar pattern
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Roving tabindex with a single tab stop, visible focus, focus return on dismissal, aria-checked for stateful items.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Implemented verbatim in the ARIA half (setTopFocus roving tabindex, Escape returns focus to the invoking top-level item, aria-checked bookkeeping for radio and checkbox items).

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive control panel narrow mobile no horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: auto-fit minmax grids with min-width:0 children for side-by-side panels that stack on narrow viewports.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: compare-grid uses repeat(auto-fit,minmax(280px,1fr)) with min-width:0 and collapses to one column under 640px; measured 0 overflow at true 360 with menus open.

openQuestions.title: Record a native-vs-ARIA keyboard trace on a flagged 143+ build
openQuestions.detail: Once a MenuElements-capable Chrome is available, drive both halves with the same key sequence and log the differences (e.g. native focus-into-menu on open, Tab behavior) so the comparison table's native column carries observed evidence rather than explainer-derived claims.

openQuestions.title: Consider typeahead (character search) in the ARIA fallback
openQuestions.detail: APG lists printable-character typeahead as optional menubar behavior; the fallback omits it, which slightly understates the real cost of the today-pattern. Adding it would make the ~120-lines comparison even more honest.

summary: Side-by-side of the free native contract vs the hand-built ARIA menubar the platform is replacing, with the ARIA half fully functional in every browser. Autorun-verified in headless Chromium 141: menus open, checkbox toggles, focus ring visible, aria-expanded/data-open in the DOM, console clean, 0 overflow at true 360.
